steps.prompt: Look at the vehicle in this driveway image. Identify it by make/body style and color. Answer with exactly one of: GREY_VAN, BLACK_TACOMA, OTHER.

These frames follow a grey van parking in the driveway. Does a person in a reflective vest get out, take a package from the van, and head toward the house? Answer exactly one of: DELIVERY_IN_PROGRESS, PERSON_NO_PACKAGE, NOBODY_YET.

This clip shows a delivery driver at the front of a house. Watch the whole clip. Did the driver bring a package TO the house and leave it there, or take a package AWAY from the house, or neither? Picking a package out of the delivery van counts as bringing it. Answer exactly one of: DELIVERED, TAKEN, NEITHER.

action.message: A package was taken from the porch
Delivery driver visited, no package seen

steps.prompt:
These frames, in time order, follow a black Tacoma pickup that has just parked facing the camera. Its driver's door is on the far side, hidden by the truck. The door on the near side, facing the camera, is the passenger door. A driver who gets out is first seen behind the truck bed or tailgate, walking around the truck.
Who got out of the driver's door? Look only for people standing or walking OUTSIDE the truck.
Write one short sentence saying who is outside the truck, then end with exactly one of these labels:
NOBODY_YET - nobody is outside the truck yet (use this when unsure)
MAN_DRIVER_SIDE - a man got out on the driver's side
WOMAN_DRIVER_SIDE - a woman got out on the driver's side
PASSENGER_ONLY - the only person you can see got out of the near-side passenger door

This clip shows a black pickup truck that has just parked in a driveway. Watch the whole clip. How many people get out of the truck, and do they walk toward the house? Answer exactly one of: ONE_TO_HOUSE, TWO_TO_HOUSE, NOBODY_LEFT_TRUCK.

action.message: Sister-in-law and her husband are at the door

chains.comment: Deliberately NO escalation steps: finger-count gestures are cheap-model territory (MediaPipe hand landmarks on CPU), so the action fires one-shot at tier-1. held_frames is the intent filter — a signal held toward the camera, not a passing hand position. Demonstrates that the tier boundary is empirical: conditions live at the cheapest tier that can handle them.
